races.name: eventmasters.co.uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: In-form six-year-old who has won twice and placed four times from 15 similar-ground starts; confirmed front runner who is likely to lead unmolested, though technically racing slightly out of profile as a Prominent-tagged horse used in the Lead role here — the key pace anchor for the whole race.|
runners_data.comment: Alpha Capture was runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back, with two more thirds further back in that sequence. He has run over today's trip and going before and rates third of 18 on our figures, though a sixth four starts back is the one blemish on his account.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a concerning recent run string showing nothing better than fifth from five recent starts on good ground; Daniel Tudhope can give her every chance but the form does not inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has run over today's trip and going before, and returns 18 days on from a seventh last time out. He has been sixth twice and seventh twice in his last five starts, winless throughout, which leaves him with plenty to find in this field.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding whose last five results read 6-11-12-6-15, all on similar ground; the headgear (hood) hasn't unlocked improvement and a five-pound claimer up doesn't compensate for the poor form cycle.|
runners_data.comment: Lord Bertie tops our figures in this field of 18, with one of the fastest speed figures on offer, and has raced over today's trip before. His recent finishes have been modest, winless in his last five starts, but on figures alone he rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Jonny Concrete
runners_data.note: Consistent front-end performer with a solid good-ground record, twice winning from 15 similar starts, but steps up to 7f from recent 6f efforts; if he gets his position early he is a factor but must prove the extra furlong.|
runners_data.comment: Jonny Concrete has run over today's trip and going before, and was runner-up three starts back, without a win in his last five starts. Ranked fourth of 18 on our figures with a strong speed figure, the two runs since that placing have been steady rather than spectacular.

runners_data.name: Mr King
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was a 7f winner 38 days ago and has a useful weight from OR 78 down to 64 range finishes; however the finishing-fade flag is a real concern and the 38-day gap needs monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Mr King won last time out, his only win in his last five starts, after finishing seventh and sixth in the two runs before that. A refusal further back is the blot on the sequence, but he returns off a 38-day break having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Stratocracy
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won over 7f at Southwell and placed five times on good-going equivalent; drops to a competitive mark and Joanna Mason rides confidently, but five consecutive below-par runs on soft-to-good ground slow the enthusiasm.|
runners_data.comment: Stratocracy won four starts back with a third five starts back before it, but has since faded to fifth in each of his last two starts. He has run over today trip and going before, returning 22 days on, with that modest recent form the main query.

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Highly progressive prominent type who has won three and placed three of his last six starts; strong record on good ground and two recent wins over 8f suggest he stays well, making him one of the best-placed horses if the race unfolds in front.|
runners_data.comment: Roaring Ralph has won four of his last six starts, with back-to-back wins before a third last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before. Eye-catching form, but our figures rate him only sixteenth of 18 in this field, some way below his official mark.

runners_data.name: Quest For Fun
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner with two places from ten good-ground runs in similar trips; Tim Easterby yard in good nick but a recent string of 9-5-5-5 finishes suggests he finds winning elusive.|
runners_data.comment: Quest For Fun rates second of 18 on our figures, comfortably above his official mark, with a third two starts back, and experience of today's trip and going. He is quick back within a fortnight, but a blank finish last time out is the one blemish on the profile.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Prominent sort with decent placed form on good ground, though his last effort was a 12th; the headgear (p) is retained and a 13-day turnaround for Easterby is sharp but the inconsistency is hard to trust.|
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last six, Mister Sox was runner-up two starts back and third three starts back but could finish only down the field last time out. He has run over today trip and going before, quick back within a fortnight, with a strong speed figure the main plus.

runners_data.name: Golden Strike
runners_data.note: Recently won over 7f on good ground at OR 75 and has two additional placed efforts from four starts on going faster than soft; Oisin Orr is a strong booking and the visor (v) has sharpened him — well-placed for this.|
runners_data.comment: Golden Strike won two starts back and also six starts back, with two runner-up finishes and a blank run in between. He has run over today's trip before, but a seventh last time out and a 27-day gap temper the case.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Bondy
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Geoff Oldroyd yard with a win on Tapeta and eight of his last ten runs on good-going variants ending in 8th or worse; form on similar turf ground is thin and the 15-day return needs to be better.|
runners_data.comment: Monsieur Bondy was a winner five starts back, but has since managed no better than a seventh, followed by two unplaced efforts and an eighth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, quick back inside three weeks, though the recent sequence makes him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Royal Accord
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who has been displaced to midfield on the map because the field is loaded with front-end types; 283-day absence is a significant concern and the yard's 0/2 recent form adds hesitation despite useful course-going form.|
runners_data.comment: Royal Accord was runner-up last time out, and a winner three starts back, with another runner-up finish among his last five starts too. He has run over today's trip and going before, but the clear concern is a 283-day absence since that latest run, leaving him fourteenth of 18 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who naturally wants to race prominently but is squeezed back on the shape by the volume of pace horses; the 51-day gap, a record of 0/3 places from eight good-ground runs, and his advancing age make this a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Fortamour was runner-up two starts back, but is without a win in his last five starts, including a seventh last time out. He rates fifth of 18 on our figures, well above his official mark, and has run over today's trip and going before after 51 days off.

runners_data.name: Orne
runners_data.note: Hold-up gelding who has placed twice from nine good-ground efforts and wears a hood; the four-and-a-half week freshener could help and two third-place finishes over 7f on good ground are the most relevant positives.|
runners_data.comment: Orne is without a win in his last five starts, but has been fairly consistent, with two thirds among them either side of a blank run. He rates well above his official mark on our figures, backed by a strong speed figure, having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has won and placed on good ground and whose natural hold-up style has been pushed forward on the map; the true closer profile — placed three times from eight good-ground starts — suits a scenario where pace is honest, but the redistribution means he may not get far back enough to deliver a clean late run.|
runners_data.comment: Ashen was runner-up last time out, and a winner four starts back, with two more thirds among his last six starts, and has run over today's trip and going before. The figures still only place him fifteenth of 18, though, despite a fair recent placing record.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Filled with winning form at OR 67 including three wins from 11 good-ground starts; a true hold-up horse bumped onto the midfield map, and if she can find clear running down the outside in the straight the class in hand could be significant.|
runners_data.comment: Invincible Ruby was a winner last time out, and a winner three starts back too, with experience of today's trip and going, but two unplaced efforts further back and a rating below her official mark leave her only seventeenth of 18 in this field.

runners_data.name: Intervention
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who has not won on good ground in 15 attempts and whose redistribution from hold-up to midfield further complicates a pattern of double-figure finishes; the form string of 4-0-0-8-7-7 is discouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Intervention is without a win in his last six starts, with a best of fourth in that sequence, and has run over today's trip and going before. His speed figure stands out at 84, but the yard is out of form, without a winner from 22 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Young horse with two wins on good ground over 6f and placed at 7f on Tapeta; wears a visor, has a 44-day gap, and his true rear-of-field style has been pushed forward on the map — if the step to 7f on fast turf suits him he is a lively long-shot.|
runners_data.comment: Jet Warrior was a winner three and four starts back, sandwiched either side by thirds, and has run over today's trip and going before. He sits bottom of our figures in this field of 18, and returns off a 44-day break with a modest fourth last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Alpha Capture is the one confirmed front runner here and, with a clear path from the gates, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable pace on Good to Firm ground without any serious immediate challenger for the lead. Behind him, Jonny Concrete, Stratocracy, Roaring Ralph, Quest For Fun, Mister Sox and Golden Strike are all genuine prominent types who will push to race close up, creating a contested group just off the pace rather than a bunched cavalry charge. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Royal Accord and Fortamour are true prominent horses shuffled back on the map, and the most likely to actually hold a forward berth are Roaring Ralph and Golden Strike given their in-form profiles and recent good-ground course experience. With Alpha Capture able to dictate a fair-but-honest gallop and the ground riding fast, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace in the slipstream of the leader — prominent racers with a finishing kick are best placed, while true hold-up horses pushed wide or back will have ground to make up on a flat, sharp-finishing track where York's straight rewards those already in contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpha Capture Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture leads without serious early pressure and sets a controlled, honest gallop into the straight.
scenarios.body: Alpha Capture controls fractions, and the horses best able to track him in the first two — Roaring Ralph, Golden Strike — arrive with a decisive advantage as the pace is steady enough to sustain an effort through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Battle
scenarios.trigger: If three or more prominent types contest the early lead forcing a genuinely hot pace from the front.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop burns off those up close and the race is taken apart by the prominent horses with the most stamina and class, those settled just a length or two off but not burning energy in the scrap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Runners Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough throughout to see the front group tie up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses settled in midfield with a strong late kick get a clear run through as leaders flatten, and genuine closers with good ground form find the conditions suit their style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Farther Back Land It
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses in mid-race, creating a stop-start gallop that compresses the field.
scenarios.body: True hold-up horses who are redistributed on the map and forced wider end up finishing fast through a tightly bunched field where gaps open late.

watchPoints.text: Royal Accord's 283-day absence is the single biggest risk factor in the race — monitor closely for any market move as a positive comeback would dramatically alter the pace map if he pushes forward early as his style suggests.

Roaring Ralph has won three of his last six and has the best recent form record among the prominent types — if he tracks Alpha Capture in second or third from the start he becomes a serious threat in the straight.

Invincible Ruby and Jet Warrior are both true hold-up horses mapped into midfield; watch the draw and early positioning because if they are forced wider than ideal they lose their main tactical edge in this shape.

Alpha Capture's actual starting behaviour is the pace key for the whole race — if he misses the break or a rival like Jonny Concrete beats him to the front, the controlled gallop scenario collapses and the race shape changes entirely.

Golden Strike wears a visor for the fifth time and has placed on his last two starts at this trip; if Oisin Orr positions him in the front group from an early stage rather than letting him drift back, he could be the one horse who benefits from the pace map without taking excessive risk.

races.name: Elevator Company Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Talismans Time
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back course winner over shorter trips who steps up sharply in trip here; Edward Bethell in 5/30 form over 14 days and Cian Horgan (5) takes 3lb, but the key question is whether this OR=82 horse can truly stay 2m½f — the style fit score of 0.93 reflects that his natural prominent profile is being stretched in this field, though the uncontested lead may compensate.
runners_data.comment: Talismans Time was a winner four and five starts back, before a blank run and a pulled-up effort, finishing third last time out. He has run over today's going before and rates second of 13 on our figures, though the interrupted sequence since those wins is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Midnight Rumble
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners this hold-up stayer whose last five runs are exclusively at 11-16f on good or standard; no wins in 15 good-ground starts is a concern on today's fast surface, and from the rear of a 14-runner field over this trip he needs the pace to collapse late to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Rumble is without a win in his last six starts, but has been admirably consistent, with two thirds and a runner-up finish among them, including a third last time out. He has run over today's trip before and rates well above his official mark, third of 13 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Venezuelan
runners_data.note: A visor-wearing prominent type who ran four consecutive placed efforts at 12-16f before two disappointing efforts; the good-to-firm surface is well within his compass across eight similar-ground runs, but Gary Hanmer's yard are only 2/10 over 14 days and the headgear hasn't been unlocking the talent of late.
runners_data.comment: Venezuelan tops our figures in this field of 13, with two runner-up finishes among his last five starts, and experience of today's trip and going. He is without a win in that spell and returns quickly within a fortnight, but on figures alone he rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Trojan Sun
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's consistent stayer won over 14f on good recently and has placed four times in similar conditions; fitted with a hood today and tackling the step to 2m½f, Paul Mulrennan picks up the ride — his positive jumping style and course familiarity over 16f give him every chance of sitting prominently and grinding out a place.
runners_data.comment: Trojan Sun was a winner three starts back, and has followed up with a sixth and a third in his last two starts. He has run over today's trip and going before and is quick back within a fortnight, though the mixed form further back, including an eighth, leaves him only sixth of 13 on our figures.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has been exposed as inconsistent — just one win from 12 good-ground starts in a prominent style; Oisin Orr's presence adds interest and he did win over 16f on standard, but two blanks at 16-18f on good suggest the 2m½f trip and going combination are against him.

runners_data.name: Rogue Empire
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins including two at 2m on good give this lightly-raced 4yo a compelling profile for today's conditions; OR=74 may be a lenient assessment after that hat-trick and Owen Lewis (5) claims 3lb, though the stable's 0/9 return in the past 14 days is a mild dampener on confidence.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Empire has won three of his last five starts, including his last three in a row, and has run over today's trip before. Eye-catching form, but a modest speed figure leaves him only seventh of 13 on our figures for this test.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: John Berry's 7yo is a genuine course performer who won over 17f on good here and has placed at 16f on good ground twice more in his last five; Kieran Shoemark knows the track, the headgear (blinkers) sharpens him, and the prominent style is perfectly aligned with today's race shape from his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Tarbat Ness was a winner last time out, and a third in the run before that, though the finishes further back have been modest. He has run over today's trip and going before and sits eighth of 13 on our figures, in line with his official mark.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner who has won at 16f on good, Tim Easterby's 4yo can't get his preferred lead position today with Talismans Time in the field — mapped to midfield, but will likely be pressing towards the front regardless; David Allan partnering, and the 8/68 trainer strike rate over 14 days is excellent, but racing out of role tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Treasure Islands was a winner three starts back, having been third and a runner-up in the two runs before that, and has won twice in his last six starts overall. He has run over today's trip and going before, but a sixth last time out and a blank run before it are the recent blemishes.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides this hold-up stayer for a small operation that rarely saddles runners; placed four times in nine good-ground starts including a 16f win on good recently, and the trip holds no fears — the main interest is whether she can produce a run from the rear in a race where the pace might not be hot enough to suit.
runners_data.comment: Valley Of Flowers was a winner two starts back, sandwiched by two fourth-place finishes either side, and has run over today's trip and going before. She returns quickly within a fortnight, though the finishes further back, including a seventh, keep this a modest overall picture.

runners_data.name: Vaguely Royal
runners_data.note: William Buick taking the mount is an immediate upgrade in class for Ian Williams' 6yo, who won over 14f on good and has placed three times at 16-17f in similar conditions; OR=69 looks lenient if he's on a going day, and the hold-up style means he needs runners to tire ahead — Buick's race-reading ability is crucial here.
runners_data.comment: Vaguely Royal won last time out but was sixth two starts back, sandwiched between that win and a run of three straight thirds further back. He has run over today's trip and going before and rates well above his official mark on our figures, fourth of 13.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up stayer running out of his natural position — mapped to midfield here but trained by Jim Goldie (3/47 past 14 days) alongside stablemate Trojan Sun; yet to win in 10 good-ground starts and last five form figures show a decline in form, so the style displacement and modest current level make him hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Furhaan was runner-up last time out, but is without a win in his last five starts, with finishes from fifth to ninth before that. He has run over today's trip and going before and rates above his official mark, though only tenth of 13 in this field.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) takes the ride on Sara Ender's improving 4yo who won over 14f on good 15 days ago; the step to 2m½f is a significant query on pedigree and form, but she's been progressive through shorter staying trips and good ground is confirmed as her best surface with 1/4 placed in similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Nanny Park was a winner last time out, and a third in the run before that, but the two starts further back yielded only a seventh and a blank run. She has run over today's going before and rates above her official mark, though only eleventh of 13 in this field.

runners_data.name: Newport
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 6yo is a natural prominent type who won over 16f on good but cannot get his preferred position today — the style-fit note confirms he'll be further back than ideal; blinkers fitted, Jardine has 2/16 over 14 days, but a long break (2021 last flat win) and the redistribution away from his natural role both weigh against him at first glance.
runners_data.comment: Newport is without a win in his last five starts, though he was a third five starts back and a fourth in the run after that, showing he can play a minor role. He returns off a 24-day break rated above his official mark, but only twelfth of 13 in this field.

runners_data.name: Queen Roslyn
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 5yo carries a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to the congested rear; recent form shows two zeros on good ground which is concerning, though she did win over 17f on soft and placed over 20f — today's good-to-firm conditions look against her based on a 1/6 record in similar going.
runners_data.comment: Queen Roslyn was a winner four and five starts back, before finishing fifth, and then unplaced in each of her last two starts. She has run over today's trip and going before and returns within a fortnight, but sits bottom of our figures in this field of 13.

races.paceDynamic: Talismans Time is the confirmed front-runner here, a single uncontested pace-setter over 2m½f on good-to-firm ground at York — a combination that sets up a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a gruelling war of attrition. With no genuine challenger willing or able to press Talismans Time from the front, Cian Horgan (5) can dictate terms and set a rhythm that plays directly into the hands of horses able to travel prominently and attack from a winning position, rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear. The field does contain more prominent-running types than the race shape can accommodate: Treasure Islands and Newport are natural prominent racers who are mapped to midfield because they cannot all secure their preferred pitch simultaneously, with Talismans Time and the likes of Rogue Empire, Tarbat Ness and Trojan Sun most likely to actually control the early positions. A steadily-run but honest pace over this extreme trip, with one genuine front-runner controlling proceedings on fast ground, strongly favours prominent racers and those positioned in the first half of the field who can stalk the leader and strike from a winning position in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Talismans Time dictates a sustainable gallop unchallenged and prominent stalkers can strike at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Rogue Empire's hat-trick of wins at 2m and his ability to sit just off the pace make him ideally suited to tracking the leader and powering clear; Tarbat Ness, a recent course winner over 17f on good, has the tactical pace to hold a handy position and get first run on the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Home Alone
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely pedestrian and Talismans Time steals an uncontested advantage that the field fails to reel in.
scenarios.body: At 2m½f on fast ground with a lone front-runner and no challenger, Talismans Time's stamina at this sort of trip means he could simply be too far ahead turning in; the hold-up types and redistributed midfield horses, not running in their natural style, are poorly placed to mount a sustained closing challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race — perhaps Rogue Empire or Trojan Sun force it — burning off the leaders and allowing genuine hold-up types to come through.
scenarios.body: Vaguely Royal, handled by William Buick and a recent winner at 14f on good, has the class and jockey to produce a late run if the tempo ensures the field is strung out; Valley Of Flowers showed a willing attitude when fourth at 16f on good and could stay on if the race truly tests stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Redistribution Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If several prominent types fight for position early and the pace becomes too pressured for the front-runner to maintain his advantage.
scenarios.body: The presence of multiple natural front-runners — Treasure Islands and Newport forced out of their best positions — risks early scrimmaging that disrupts the settled shape and opens the door for a horse like Nanny Park, a fresh 15-day-ago winner who stays well, to emerge from a handy position; however this scenario is inherently low probability because the redistribution itself suggests those horses will be unable to impose their will.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Empire's hat-trick at 2m on good makes him a genuine threat if he can stalk Talismans Time and produce his finishing effort turning into the straight — watch whether Owen Lewis (5) can place him in the first four early.

Treasure Islands and Newport are both natural front-runners who cannot get to the front today; if either pushes forward aggressively in the first half-mile, they could inject unwanted tempo into an otherwise controlled race and unsettle the front-runner's rhythm.

William Buick's booking on Vaguely Royal (OR=69) stands out as a significant market mover — if support appears before the off, the Buick factor combined with the horse's placed form at 14-17f on good could make him a late-closing danger to the prominent stalkers.

The step to 2m½f is an unproven distance for several runners including Nanny Park and Rogue Empire — monitor market confidence in those two specifically, as each has only raced at a maximum of 16f and stamina resolution at this trip is not guaranteed.

races.name: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Diplomacy
runners_data.note: Debutant for Michael & David Easterby with Billy Garritty up — yard in reasonable recent form (3/26 in 14 days) and the unknown factor on debut means no style profile can be pinned down; watch market moves carefully.

runners_data.name: Rule Of The Agency
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up specialist returns after 38 days; genuinely wants to be last and deliver late, but the race map places it in midfield — its chance is tempered by racing away from its preferred hunting ground, and its sole similar-going run produced a seventh.

runners_data.name: The First Drop
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's gelding is the sole confirmed pace-setter here and should control this 7f uncontested; ran second over 7f Good ground last time and the ability to dictate solo on a flat galloping track is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Rocket
runners_data.note: Carried a fades-in-finish flag alongside an eighth on its only Good-ground 7f start; Joanna Mason rides for the Easterby yard but the tendency to weaken late is a concern in a race where a late effort is needed from further back.

runners_data.name: Special Operations
runners_data.note: Another debut runner for Tim Easterby, drawn into a race where the yard has strong current momentum (8/68 over 14 days); style and ability completely unknown, but Sean Kirrane is an experienced conditional who will place the horse sensibly.

runners_data.name: Sweet Iris
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partners this Fahey-trained filly who faded to tenth over 6f Good ground on debut; the step to 7f could help but the finish flag is a real concern, and Good To Firm York is a demanding test for a horse still finding its stride.

runners_data.name: Travellers Girl
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's filly has form figures of 4-3-3 over 6f Good, stepping up to 7f today for the first time; Kevin Stott rides and the extra furlong is an open question — placed consistently but has not beaten many and OR of 70 is the lowest in the field.

runners_data.name: Coral Cove
runners_data.note: James Owen's colt was second over 7f Good ground on its only start and slots naturally into a prominent tracking role behind The First Drop; Kieran Shoemark is a high-quality booking and the horse's profile fits this race shape as well as any in the field.

races.paceDynamic: The First Drop is the one confirmed front-runner in this 7f Good To Firm York contest and, with no genuine rival likely to push it for the lead, should control proceedings at a sustainable gallop from the off. Coral Cove is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and will likely slot in directly behind, meaning the pace is unlikely to be searingly fast — a measured, even tempo is the most probable outcome over this straight seven furlongs. Rule Of The Agency is a genuine hold-up type that has been mapped to midfield purely because the rear of the field is not as congested as the horse's natural position would suggest; it will not be racing in its truest comfort zone. This race shape — a lone leader setting a controlled, uncontested pace over a flat, galloping track — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types who can travel just off the pace and pick up efficiently, rather than deep closers who need a strong tempo to deliver their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If The First Drop dictates an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the prominent stalkers travel smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: The First Drop sets a fair but unflustered pace, and a horse sitting second or third with cover can pounce inside the final two furlongs without needing a strong pace injection from the front; the flat York straight rewards those who have saved energy mid-race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to string the field out and a well-positioned midfielders can unleash a sustained run.
scenarios.body: A slightly more honest gallop stretches the field and creates a gap for a horse sitting fourth or fifth at halfway to pick off tired rivals in the final furlong; Good To Firm ground suits those with a clean, economical action.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two unknown debutants (Diplomacy or Special Operations) shows superior raw ability and powers clear from a prominent pitch.
scenarios.body: A first-time starter unburdened by a tactical profile can exploit an unfussy gallop, and Michael & David Easterby and Tim Easterby both have strong yard form in the current 14-day window suggesting juveniles are ready to run; Good To Firm is a fair test of raw ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and hold-up types swoop late, noting this depends on horses racing out of role.
scenarios.body: Rule Of The Agency and The Resdev Rocket would need a genuine strong pace to be produced with a late run, but both carry the burden of being out of their natural positions and of fading in the finish respectively; this scenario is materially less likely because the true closers are not truly anchored at the rear.

watchPoints.text: The First Drop's ability to dictate solo is the single biggest tactical factor — watch whether it is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the gates or whether Coral Cove applies early pressure to change the race shape.
Both Diplomacy and Special Operations are debutants from yards in form; significant market support for either at the off should be treated as live information given neither has a known style profile.
Rule Of The Agency is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield role — if it pulls hard or becomes unsettled racing out of character, it is likely to underperform its odds significantly.

The Resdev Rocket and Sweet Iris both carry a fades-in-finish flag from their last runs; if either is prominent early and beginning to weaken at the two-furlong pole, closers from behind them may have more opportunity than the pace map initially suggests.

Travellers Girl steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time — watch how Kevin Stott positions her in the early stages, as a filly who has placed consistently at the shorter trip may settle better with the extra distance or alternatively be caught flat-footed if the pace quickens.

races.name: Tomahawk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Glory Hyde
runners_data.note: Consistent 6f front-runner with four wins on Good ground, dropping back in trip slightly from recent outings — Roger Fell's filly is ideally placed to exploit an uncontested lead if connections allow her to roll from the front, though a STYLE_FIT flag notes she is technically mapped as prominent rather than full lead.
runners_data.comment: Glory Hyde was unplaced last time out but that follows four wins in her last six starts, and she has run over today's trip and going before. A rating of 77 leaves her only mid-pack in a field of 22, though a 13-day break keeps her fresh.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this David O'Meara 4yo who races from the rear, with strong similar-going stats (13/15) suggesting the surface is no concern — the difficulty is 6f at York rarely gives genuine hold-up types the run of their lives in a sustainable-pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Tiva is winless in her last five starts, though a second four starts back shows she's competitive, and she has run over today's trip and going before. Freshened by a 21-day break, a rating of 82 puts her among the leading names here despite modest recent finishes.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old Paul Midgley veteran whose recent form shows a distant win in a Goodwood race amid some modest efforts; hold-up style and a 41-day break mean he will need everything to fall right on what is only his sixth run at this distance on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Grant Wood heads our figures on a rating of 86, with a win six starts back and experience over today's trip and going. He was unplaced in each of his last two outings though, and a 41-day break adds to the fitness question.

runners_data.name: Raatea
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old Julie Camacho sprinter returning from a 134-day absence, fitted with hood and headstall — the long layoff is a significant concern in a field of 22 and his similar-going figures on Soft/Standard skew rather than Good mean this faster surface is relatively unexplored territory.
runners_data.comment: Raatea was fifth last time out but that followed a third and a second, with a win five starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before. A 134-day absence is the obvious concern, though a rating of 83 makes him one of the leading players here.

runners_data.name: Almarada Prince
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners this Paul Midgley 5yo who has placed four times in the last six runs without winning — back-of-field style will need the race to be run at a genuine clip to allow him to close, which the expected pace shape does not guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Almarada Prince has trended the right way, finishing third then fourth in his last two starts, a clear improvement on the run before that, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Back within 13 days and rated 85, he's our pick despite being winless in his last six.

runners_data.name: Aberama Gold
runners_data.note: Conor Whiteley takes the mount on this David O'Meara veteran wearing a visor, with back-to-back runner-up finishes on Good ground in recent outings suggesting he is in solid form — but as a hold-up horse facing 22 runners, getting a clear run at the right moment remains the central challenge.
runners_data.comment: Aberama Gold has been runner-up in each of his last two starts and quick to back that up again just nine days later, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour. A rating of 85 puts him right in the mix, though he remains without a win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: HK Fourteen
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby rides for Tony Carroll, who has five winners from 31 runners in the 14-day window; this 6yo is better suited to 5f on Good ground (three wins) but is not without a shout if allowed a prominent position and the pace sets up kindly from the front.
runners_data.comment: HK Fourteen won five starts back but has been below that level since, sixth last time out having also finished unplaced twice in between. He has run over today's trip and going before, though a 53-day break and a rating of 76 leave him only mid-pack in this field.

runners_data.name: Rajaking
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark takes the ride on this T J Kent 4yo — form figures of 3-4-6 on Good ground at 6f suggest he runs his race consistently enough but without quite finding extra late on, which mirrors the hold-up style and the likelihood of a midfield position in a busy 22-runner sprint.
runners_data.comment: Rajaking is winless in his last five starts but has trended the right way, third last time out following finishes of fourth, sixth, seventh and ninth before that. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a 20-day break keeps him fresh, though a rating of 77 leaves him only mid-pack.

runners_data.name: Magic Boy
runners_data.note: P J McDonald partners this Nigel Tinkler 4yo with a 10/10 strike rate on Good ground and a win last time out at 6f — prominent style and excellent going record make him one of the best-placed horses tactically, and recent form is strong enough to make him a serious player if he can track Glory Hyde from a handy pitch.
runners_data.comment: Magic Boy won last time out and has two wins in his last five, the other four starts back, with a second and a fourth also in the mix. He has run over today trip and going before, back in 13 days and rated 81, an eighth five starts back his only blemish.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: James Sullivan partners Ruth Carr's 7yo who has shown on-pace ability at exactly this course and distance on Good ground — modest form at 0 last time but wins at 6f Good earlier in the sequence suggest he remains capable, and his prominent style suits the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: Fiscal Policy was unplaced last time out but that follows a second and a third in the two starts before, plus a win four starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Back within 13 days and rated 79, he sits mid-table on paper despite the below-par finish last time.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 7yo has not run for 168 days, races at 7f in his history rather than 6f, and is flagged as fading in the finish — a combination of long layoff, trip concern and finishing style makes him hard to recommend in a 22-runner sprint.
runners_data.comment: Tolstoy is winless in his last five starts and was unplaced last time out, though he has run over today's trip and going before. A 168-day absence is the major concern, but a rating of 82, well above his official mark, hints at more to come if fitness allows.

runners_data.name: Alpha Magic
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a notable jockey booking but this Michael & David Easterby 4yo's last five runs show no better than fourth on Good ground — a true hold-up horse whose natural rear-of-field position is compromised in this busy race shape, reducing its chance of finding clear air in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Alpha Magic is winless in his last five starts, with three unplaced efforts including his latest, but he did finish fourth four starts back and has run over today's trip and going before. Back within 13 days and rated 80, above his official mark, he remains capable of better than he has shown lately.

runners_data.name: Bonnie's Boy
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partners this Richard & Peter Fahey 4yo who is better suited to 5f than 6f on the evidence of his form — a genuine hold-up type whose redistribution into midfield means he cannot settle into his preferred role, and his trip profile makes the extra furlong an additional hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Bonnie's Boy was unplaced last time out and has managed only two finishes inside the top four since a win five starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a 41-day gap since his latest run adds a fitness question, though a rating of 79 keeps him competitive in this field.

runners_data.name: Who Wants Me
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen rides for Iain Jardine — back-to-back wins at 5f and 7f on Good ground give the form some substance, and the horse wears a hood, but as a true hold-up type forced into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, getting a clean run in a 22-runner sprint is a significant practical obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Who Wants Me arrives on the back of two wins in a row, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but our figures rate her bottom of this field, below her official mark of 73. Sixth and fourth came before those victories, tempering how much stock to put in the recent upturn.

runners_data.name: Beattie Is Back
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (3lb claimer) takes the ride on this Richard & Peter Fahey 7yo — held up naturally but carrying race experience at 6f Good from multiple angles; form shows a second place at 7f which is slightly too far back in the sequence to inspire full confidence in current form.
runners_data.comment: Beattie Is Back is winless in his last six starts, fifth last time out, though a second four starts back shows he can be competitive. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a 37-day break since his latest run leaves him only mid-pack on a rating of 76.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: Jack Garritty partners Adrian Nicholls's 5yo who carries excellent course credentials — 12/15 similar-going runs, three wins, and recent placed efforts at exactly 6f Good mean his prominent style and proven track record make him one of the most tactically well-suited runners in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ingleby Archie has been admirably consistent, third last time out and never out of the first four in his last five starts including a win two starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before. The trouble is a rating of only 72 leaves him down the field here, with more needed to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Sugar Baby
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh rides for Peter Niven, whose 14-day record is a blank from three runners — this 8yo has four wins at 6f Good and races prominently, giving her a clear tactical fit in the expected race shape, though age and a moderate in-race position behind the leader must be weighed against her solid going figures.
runners_data.comment: Sugar Baby won last time out but the form before that reads fifth, seventh, eighth and seventh, a lean spell that leaves plenty to prove. He has run over today's trip and going before, and on a rating of 75 he's up against it from well down this field of 22.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie takes the ride on this Philip Kirby 4yo — a genuine hold-up horse whose deep-field position is compromised in a race with this many natural closers; the last run was a distant 14th at 6f Good and the form figures on soft/standard rather than fast ground are the more encouraging ones.
runners_data.comment: Educating Rita is winless in her last five starts and has been unplaced in each of her last two, though a third three starts back shows she has more in her locker. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 80, well clear of her official mark, hints at untapped potential.

runners_data.name: Dicko The Legend
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty rides this Liam Bailey 6yo who ran just seven days ago — consistent form figures of 3-4-5-6 at 6f Good show he runs his race but rarely wins, and though he prefers to come from behind, the redistribution means he cannot reproduce his natural hold-up run here.
runners_data.comment: Dicko The Legend is winless in his last six starts and sits second-from-bottom of this field on a rating of 71, though a second six starts back and a quick return just seven days after his latest run are the redeeming features. He has run over today's trip and going before, but leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Alex Jary (3lb claimer) rides for Antony Brittain — only four runs on Good or similar out of fifteen and no wins on the going are significant concerns, and as a hold-up type compressed into midfield, he faces a difficult task to get competitive in a 22-runner sprint on ground he has rarely handled.
runners_data.comment: Tough Enough is winless in his last five, the highlight a second four starts back among finishes of fourth, sixth and two unplaced efforts. He has run over today trip and going before, and on a rating of 72 he faces an uphill task in this field of 22.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: David Allan partners Tim Easterby's 6yo — consistent placed form at 5f Good (three thirds in sequence) but stepping up to 6f here, wearing hood, as a natural hold-up horse in a race that is unlikely to play to his strengths; his best efforts have come over shorter.
runners_data.comment: Spirit Of Applause is the model of consistency, four thirds and a fourth across his last five starts, yet stays winless. He has run over today trip and going before, and a rating of 73 makes him hard to dismiss, even if turning places into a win is the question.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Jack Nicholls (5lb claimer) rides this Liam Bailey 5yo who ran seven days ago with a win two runs back at 6f Good — wears tongue tie, genuine hold-up style, but compressed into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, meaning his finishing effort will depend on finding daylight in the final furlong that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Dorney Lake has found form quickly, second last time out following a win two starts back, a big step up on the finishes before that. He has run over today's trip and going before, and though a rating of 72 leaves him down this field of 22, the upward trend and a rapid seven-day turnaround are in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Glory Hyde is the one confirmed front-runner and will stride to the front from the off, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 6f at York — a track that rewards those who travel well and quicken in the final two furlongs rather than grinding out. HK Fourteen, Magic Boy, Fiscal Policy, Ingleby Archie and Sugar Baby will press for prominent positions behind her, creating a moderately competitive early pace but not a truly searching one, meaning the lead is unlikely to be pressured into self-destruction. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Alpha Magic, Who Wants Me, Bonnie's Boy, Beattie Is Back, Educating Rita and others are all true hold-up types forced into midfield roles where they cannot express their natural closing ability, materially weakening the late-pace threat. This race shape — a sustainable, uncontested lead with a competitive but not frenetic mid-race pace on fast ground — strongly favours prominent-racing types who can track the leader and produce a clean turn of foot in the closing stages, rather than genuine closers who need a truly run race to make up ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Glory Hyde bowls along at a sustainable clip and prominent rivals Magic Boy, Ingleby Archie and Fiscal Policy track her without being overly pressured.
scenarios.body: Glory Hyde leads into the final furlong and the race develops into a sustained drive from the top four or five, with Magic Boy and Ingleby Archie best placed to pounce having traveled within two lengths throughout. This scenario suits horses with a 6f prominent profile on Good to Firm York ground — Magic Boy's in-form record and Ingleby Archie's strong course-and-distance stats make them the chief beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely uncontested and Glory Hyde is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, controlling tempo and stealing a decisive lead entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to challenge for the front, Glory Hyde rolls clear from the 2f marker and her rivals are left chasing a shadow into the rising finish at York. Her four wins on Good ground over 6f and her habit of front-running efficiently make her the standout beneficiary of a slow-burn lead scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a few compact, well-positioned midfielders find a gap to finish through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Horses like Aberama Gold and Almarada Prince — both suited to 6f on Good ground and holding a hold-up profile that becomes effective mid-race when there is some pace — could capitalise if the early pace quickens unexpectedly. This scenario requires a more contested early fractions than the race shape currently suggests, making it a secondary possibility rather than the default read.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race develops into a true sprint finish and the redistribution of hold-up horses into midfield accidentally gives them a race-pace they can exploit.
scenarios.body: The probability here is materially discounted because the horses most likely to win this shape — Who Wants Me, Bonnie's Boy, Alpha Magic — are all tagged as redistributed true hold-up types who are unlikely to be in their natural rear-of-field position and therefore cannot produce their best finishing effort. Even if late pace emerges, these horses face the double disadvantage of racing out of role on a track where position off the home turn is decisive.

watchPoints.text: Glory Hyde could exploit an uncontested lead — if no rival challenges her prominently in the first furlong, she may steal an unassailable advantage before the home turn.

Magic Boy and Ingleby Archie are the two prominent horses most likely to challenge Glory Hyde — watch whether they can get a tracking position early because their final-furlong pace depends entirely on travelling within two lengths of the leader.

With 22 runners, draw and early position are critical — horses forced wide at the start or trapped in a pocket at the 2f marker, particularly the redistributed hold-up types, face a near-impossible task to make late ground on a flat 6f York track with a sustainable pace.

races.name: British EBF Lyric Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Diamond Rain
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old has a consistent recent profile (five places from five runs including two wins) and Buick invariably lets her roll from the front; the style-fit flag is a minor caveat given she naturally wants to lead and this is exactly the position she will occupy, though her last win came over 10f and the extra half-furlong is a mild question.
runners_data.comment: Diamond Rain heads our ratings on 115 and boasts the form to match, never finishing outside the first three in her last five starts and winning the last of that sequence five starts back. With her trainer among the form yards and fresh for a 28-day break, she rates the one to beat, even without adding to that win since.

runners_data.name: Miss Justice
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's mare carries a tongue-tie and has been frustratingly consistent without winning recently, hitting the frame in 3 of her last 5 on good ground; her prominent style should place her close enough to challenge but her OR of 101 and recent fourth-placed finishes suggest she needs others to flop rather than winning on merit.
runners_data.comment: Miss Justice is the clear second string on our figures at 109, with a second four starts back her best form and experience over today's trip and going in her favour. She remains without a win in her last five starts though, and has twice finished fourth since that placed effort, leaving a small query over her finishing power.

runners_data.name: Qilin Queen
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field and her last win came over 12f on soft — the switch to faster ground and shorter trip are questions, but Kieran Shoemark can slot her in behind the pack and produce her late; a trainer hitting form at 10/42 over 14 days is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Qilin Queen ranks third on our figures at 104, with a win five starts back and experience over today's trip and going both in her favour. Her form has since dipped though, with a seventh last time out following two fourths and an unplaced run, so she needs to rediscover that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Regal Charm
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's mare has winning form on both soft and good and arrives fresh on 45 days off; though she is a natural front-runner by inclination, this field's pace architecture has pushed her into a midfield slot she would not choose, and her STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects the genuine compromise she must make to her race-craft.
runners_data.comment: Regal Charm won last time out and has two wins in her last five starts, also finishing second two starts back, and she has run over today's trip and going before. A rating of 99, well clear of her official mark, hints at more in hand, though a 45-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Estissa
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's three-year-old has a strong recent record — three wins from her last four on standard-to-fast ground — but all five of her career runs have been over 8f and this 10f trip is completely uncharted territory; she would naturally press the pace hard but cannot get there in this field, and whether she stays this longer trip is the pivotal unknown.
runners_data.comment: Estissa has a solid recent record, with two wins in her last five starts and never worse than third, and she has run over today's going before. Rated only sixth of six here though, some way below her official mark, she looks up against it on our figures despite the healthy form.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old showed Group-race potential when winning over 7f and 8f earlier this season before finishing seventh in the Ribblesdale, and she has been off 49 days; a genuine front-runner by nature, she is shoe-horned into a midfield role by Diamond Rain's presence, and Edward Greatrex must decide early whether to fight for position or settle — that decision will define her race.
runners_data.comment: On Message won three and four starts back and has run over today's trip and going before, with her trainer among the form yards at 12 winners from 43 runners lately. She was well beaten last time out, though, and a 49-day gap since raises a fitness question in this field of six.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Rain is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners over 1m2½f at York on good-to-firm ground, William Buick can dictate a controlled, metronomic pace from the front without being seriously pressured. The three redistributed horses — On Message, Estissa, and Regal Charm — are all naturally prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, but with Diamond Rain already occupying that slot, at least two of them must compromise their position and race in a more restrained fashion than they would prefer. That crowding effect behind the leader creates a compressed, tactical contest through the first mile where positions are hard-won and the race is effectively run at Diamond Rain's tempo. This shape strongly favours a horse that can track the leader in second or third without burning energy, carry enough class to quicken off a steady gallop, and see out the trip — a clean-travelling prominent type or a patient hold-up horse with a sharp turn of foot will be best positioned when the race ignites in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diamond Rain Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Rain leads uncontested at a controlled tempo, dictating every yard from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: Buick sets a sustainable pace on the front end and kicks off the home turn, giving Diamond Rain first run on every rival; the good-to-firm surface rewards her clean action and she is hard to reel in from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the crowded prominent horses finds a clean run in second or third and outstays Diamond Rain inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Regal Charm or On Message, forced to race slightly off the pace, uses that enforced restraint as a tactical advantage and unleashes a stronger late run than usual; the extra distance suits a horse that appreciates being dropped in slightly from their natural position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop From Off Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough early to string out the field and leave a gap for a genuine hold-up horse to finish through.
scenarios.body: Qilin Queen, the one confirmed hold-up runner, is able to pick off fading rivals in the closing stages as the front-runners exhaust each other; she has already won over 12f on good ground and the step up in class is offset by the pace shape playing directly into her hands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the race degenerates into a sprint finish and tactics are negated entirely.
scenarios.body: A compressed, sprint-finish scenario over a flat York mile-and-a-quarter on fast ground would bring every runner back into play, including hold-up types who lack the tactical speed to win a flat-out dash; Miss Justice and Estissa, with their prominent tendencies, are best equipped for a scrappy dash to the line.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Rain's early sectionals — if Buick eases her into a very slow first half-mile, the compressed field hands every rival an equally good chance in the dash home and her advantage evaporates.

On Message's positioning in the first two furlongs — if Greatrex tries to press Diamond Rain for the lead rather than accepting midfield, an early speed duel could burn out both front-runners and gift the race to Qilin Queen.
Estissa's stamina at the 2f pole — all her form is over 8f and a step to 10f on fast ground is an untested leap; watch if she suddenly stops when the race quickens off the turn.

Qilin Queen's early track position — coming from off the pace at York's flat straight requires a clear run; Shoemark must not get trapped wide or fail to find daylight through a bunched, prominent-heavy midfield group.

Regal Charm's freshness factor — 45 days off can sharpen or dull a horse, and Henry Candy's low 14-day strike rate (1/4) suggests the yard is not in a red-hot vein; watch her coat and paddock demeanour for signs the layoff has left her needing the run.

races.name: Sky Bet Go-Racing-In-Yorkshire Summer Festival Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter over 5½f; Tim Easterby-trained and 68 days off, which is worth watching, though course form reads adequately on good ground — her chance rests entirely on holding a lead she should have unchallenged, but the STYLE_FIT tag at 0.93 tempers confidence she can do enough once headed.
runners_data.comment: One of the leading dangers. Winless in five runs (4th, 5th, 4th, 9th, unplaced) but our rating of 87 puts her third of 12 with a speed figure of 80, and she already has today's trip and going covered; a 68-day break is the concern.

runners_data.name: Nursia
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner returns in fair trim with a win on standard ground (Southwell) over 6f; shorter 5½f trip on fast going is a slight unknown, but a clean prominent pitch behind Anaisa suits Kevin Stott's patient style and a recent third on good ground in a similar handicap is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy on our figures, bottom of the pack on 65 with a modest 66 speed figure. A winner two starts back and with today's trip covered, but the yard is out of form (1 from 21 lately) and this is a 43-day return.

runners_data.name: Kinnalargy
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up horse has shown a tendency to find trouble and finish midfield in similar good-ground 5f-6f handicaps; Oisin McSweeney takes the ride with limited opportunities from this yard in the 14-day window, and a record of 1W and 2P from 8 similar-going runs does not shout confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: Our selection, second in the rankings on 87 with a smart 86 speed figure, and has run over today's trip and going before despite being winless in five (7th, 5th, unplaced, 4th, 7th). The yard's modest recent record (1 from 21) is the only knock.

runners_data.name: Go Vince Go
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby gelding that has finished third and fourth repeatedly in similar handicap company on good ground; David Allan rides, and the horse's consistent prominent style suits this race shape well over the half-furlong shorter trip, though his strike-rate of 1W from 15 similar-going runs suggests he finds a way to get beaten.
runners_data.comment: Tops our figures on 89 with a strong 83 speed figure, and already has today's trip and going covered. Yet to win in six starts (4th, unplaced, 8th, 3rd, 4th, 8th), with a third-placed effort among them showing he can figure at this level.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on soft ground 14 days ago and is quickly back; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) rides for a small Lemos De Souza yard with 2 from 5 recently, and while the front-running intent is genuine, the rise from a soft-ground success to fast ground is a concern given only one placed run from five similar-going starts.
runners_data.comment: Solid form file for a midfield runner, rated 81 (6th of 12) with a useful 83 speed figure. A winner three starts back, with a third-placed run among the finishes, though results have varied (unplaced, 5th, 9th, 6th); he has already run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's horse has won on good ground over 6f and placed over 5f on good, giving him solid credentials for this surface; Harry Davies takes over and the horse's record of 1W and 3P from 13 similar-going runs shows he fires consistently — races prominently and likely finds a clean pitch tracking Anaisa.
runners_data.comment: Rated 79 and 7th of 12 with a 73 speed figure, a fair, consistent sort with two thirds, a second and a win (five starts back) among her recent starts. The yard is out of form (0 from 22), though she has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Dolos Dream
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 3yo has strong form figures including two wins on standard ground (Southwell) and a placed effort over 5f on good; De Sousa in the plate is a positive, and his ability to deliver a challenge is not in doubt — his actual preference to race prominently is the context here, finding himself further back than ideal given the crowded front end.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger on our figures, rated 84 (4th of 12). A winner two starts back and again four starts back, sandwiched by a third and a runner-up effort — clearly in good form; a 42-day absence and a modest 70 speed figure are the risks to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Bravo Hotel
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides for Michael & David Easterby; this hold-up filly has placed on good and soft over 5f multiple times without getting her head in front, and her profile only works if the pace is genuine enough to bring her into the race late — a steady tempo from Anaisa leaves her vulnerable.
runners_data.comment: An outsider on our figures, down in 9th of 12 on a rating of 78 with a 73 speed figure. Winless in five starts (5th, 3rd, 3rd, 5th, 3rd), though three thirds show he's rarely far away; has today's trip and going covered, but a 38-day break is a concern.

runners_data.name: Explosive Finnish
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost runner with two placed efforts over 5f on good ground in recent form; hold-up style means she needs something to go wrong in front, and while Oisin Orr is a capable jockey, four runs without a win in similar conditions question whether she has enough to finish the job.
runners_data.comment: A midfield sort rated 82 (5th of 12) with a useful 77 speed figure. Yet to win in five starts (5th, 2nd, 2nd, 3rd, 3rd) but the placings — two seconds and two thirds — show real consistency; already has today's trip and going covered, returning here after a 27-day break.

runners_data.name: Dragon Spin
runners_data.note: Hollinshead 3yo has won twice over 5f on good ground in this calendar year and has clear course-and-distance credentials; a natural front-runner who finds himself absorbed into midfield by the weight of pace in this field — his best form comes when he can stride on, and that outlet is closed here.
runners_data.comment: An outsider at 11th of 12 on our figures (74), though the 75 speed figure is a touch better than that suggests. A winner two starts back and again four starts back shows real ability, but a 6th in between highlights the inconsistency; she has already run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Liverpool Star
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby hold-up type who won over 6f on good and has placed repeatedly in similar company; Billy Garritty rides and the horse's 9 placed runs from 14 similar-going starts shows a degree of reliability, but the hold-up role is a genuine disadvantage if Anaisa keeps fractions honest rather than fast.
runners_data.comment: A midfield runner on our figures, rated 79 (8th of 12) with a modest 69 speed figure. A winner four starts back, with a third-place effort further back too, but four finishes of 4th or 5th elsewhere temper the enthusiasm; already has today's trip and going covered on a 23-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Slot
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's 3yo is back after just seven days, which is the shortest turnaround in the field and worth monitoring; a genuine prominent type by nature whose two recent placed efforts came on good ground over 6f — running back so quickly and from a mid-division berth he is unlikely to naturally occupy compounds the challenge here.
runners_data.comment: An outsider on our figures, 10th of 12 on a rating of 75 with a 70 speed figure. Winless in five (2nd, 2nd, 4th, 4th, 5th) but the two runner-up efforts show she's competitive, and a swift 7-day turnaround keeps her fresh; already has today's trip and going covered.

races.paceDynamic: Anaisa is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should control fractions on Good to Firm ground over 5½f at York — a track that can favour those who travel kindly and avoid traffic. The prominent brigade is overcrowded: Nursia, Go Vince Go, U S S Charleston, and Space Bear all want to be close to the pace, but Dolos Dream, Dragon Spin, and Slot are true prominent types who are unlikely to secure their natural position given how stacked the front of the field is, and will find themselves shuffled back into midfield. With Anaisa dictating an unchallenged rhythm, the race is unlikely to be run at a truly scorching tempo, meaning those who can race prominently and travel smoothly behind the leader will have a significant tactical advantage over genuine hold-up horses who will need the pace to quicken sharply late. This race shape firmly favours compact, prominent racers that can track the leader and produce their effort early in the straight rather than deep closers who depend on a punishing gallop to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Anaisa Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Anaisa sets an unchallenged pace and the field settles into a clean rhythm, allowing the prominent horses to travel into contention.
scenarios.body: Anaisa dictates modest fractions, the race stays together until the two-furlong pole, and horses who have tracked comfortably pounce with a sustained run rather than a sharp sprint; Space Bear, Go Vince Go, and Nursia are best placed to exploit this shape from close range. Genuine hold-up horses lack the tempo to generate momentum and arrive too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On, Anaisa Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady enough that Anaisa or the closest pursuers simply outstay the field without being reeled in.
scenarios.body: A slow-moderate pace suits the leader disproportionately on fast ground over this trip, and if no prominent horse lands a serious early challenge, Anaisa could prove hard to catch; Space Bear or Nursia press but cannot close the gap in time. This shape punishes hold-up horses severely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded prominent group causes interference and bunching in the straight, creating a gap for hold-up horses to burst through.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of Dolos Dream, Dragon Spin, and Slot into mid-division adds bodies to the middle of the race and increases the chance of shuffling late; Bravo Hotel or Explosive Finnish could benefit if daylight appears. Liverpool Star's course form over similar trips in good ground makes her a credible latecomer in this specific scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging among the prominent group results in a messy, uneven gallop that compounds the redistribution problem and scrambles the field.
scenarios.body: Dolos Dream or Dragon Spin, true front-runners forced to race out of their natural position, may find gaps earlier than expected and produce a one-paced challenge from mid-division; however, their forced role tempers confidence in them winning this shape outright. Slot's recent quick reappearance (7 days) is also a query here.

watchPoints.text: Anaisa sets a lone pace unchallenged — watch whether Sean Kirrane elects to coast in front or genuinely sets a true gallop, as that single decision dictates whether hold-up horses can ever get into this race.

The prominent group of Nursia, Go Vince Go, U S S Charleston, and Space Bear is highly congested — watch the early 1f for jostling and position losses that could compromise any of these runners' chances of landing the winning tactical pitch.

Dolos Dream and Dragon Spin are forced out of their natural prominent role by the weight of pace types; watch whether either manages to find a position closer than their mapped midfield slot, as either could be competitive if circumstances allow them forward.
U S S Charleston returns after just 14 days on ground faster than her recent win — watch for any market drift that signals the quick turnaround or ground switch is a concern for connections.

Slot runs for the second time in seven days — watch her in the paddock and early stages for any sign of staleness, as horses returning this quickly in fast-ground sprint handicaps can run flat if not fully recovered.
